I felt proud of a serving bowl I made on the pottery wheel. What I remember most is how it looked after firing—the blue glaze covering the inside and the smooth rim. Those are the details that stand out to me, rather than who was around.

It was satisfying to look at it and think, “I made that.” It wasn’t just the idea of a bowl anymore; it was an actual serving bowl, something I’d made myself. The smooth rim was a big part of it. I could look at the finished piece and feel pleased with how it had turned out. It was a quiet sort of pride.
